title: Before Borders, The World Was One Road

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide cinematic shot of ancient trade caravans crossing deserts, ships sailing across oceans, carts moving through mountain passes. No visible faces.
scenes.motion_prompt: slow cinematic glide, strong parallax, clouds drifting, flags fluttering, animals and wheels in continuous motion
scenes.narration: Long before borders existed, the world was already moving together.

scenes.visual_prompt: Medium close-up of an elderly historian walking slowly toward the camera, timeless robes, calm eyes, soft volumetric light.
scenes.motion_prompt: slow forward walk, subtle head movement, steady camera, natural speaking motion
scenes.narration: Trade connected people before politics ever divided them.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide aerial shot of ancient cities exchanging goods, glowing trade routes spreading across land and sea, no faces visible.
scenes.motion_prompt: top-down cinematic drift, glowing paths expanding, ships and caravans moving simultaneously
scenes.narration: Ideas traveled with spices, stories traveled with silk, and beliefs moved faster than armies.

scenes.visual_prompt: Medium close-up of a younger man standing still, questioning eyes, dramatic side lighting, dark background.
scenes.motion_prompt: minimal motion, subtle breathing, steady gaze into camera
scenes.narration: Then why do we believe separation came first?

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide cinematic montage of maps forming, symbols spreading, ships docking, roads glowing across continents. No faces.
scenes.motion_prompt: fast-to-slow time-lapse blend, layered parallax, expanding light trails
scenes.narration: Because history remembers walls more easily than roads.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of the witness stopping, looking directly into the camera, soft rim light defining the face.
scenes.motion_prompt: very slow forward drift, controlled facial motion
scenes.narration: But connection came first. And it always will.
